title: Canonical trace presentations and their normalized result data
statement: Use the models, restriction and direct-image comparisons of [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models], the coefficient cones of [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-coefficients], normalized Chern data of [def-sp-tower-class-chern], finite normalization of [def-sp-tower-class-finite], and geometric systems of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. A trace presentation consists of these data, the ordinary and total derived direct images at varying, discrete constant and completed coefficients, and total derived limits. The ordinary restriction/direct-image identifications are identity on underlying sections. Their derived comparisons satisfy the common-unit equation on complexes (or equivalently the specified computation on K-injectives). The limit comparison is the one induced by limit.post; the normalized coefficient and root-line limit maps are required invertible. Define the strict splitting by restricting its actual unit and Chern summands. Define the strict system trace by restricting the specified twisted inverse splitting and second projection. A completed trace is normalized when its restriction followed by the unit-limit comparison equals the limit of this system trace, under the prescribed source comparisons. Define result data to be such a presentation with invertible splitting, a normalized completed trace, the equations with every actual derived-limit projection, and the finite unit/Chern trace normalization $0,1$. This is a definition of data; existence and the diagonal identities are asserted separately by the owning trace theorem.
